subject: Discovery Recap: Reliability & Graceful Degradation
messages:
From: Sarah Jones <sarah@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from today's call — reliability focus

Ben — thanks for the demo today. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can determine next steps with the platform team: 

Pain points: 
- We had two P0 incidents in the last 9 months where model endpoints in us-west saturated and caused 30–45s tails for critical user journeys.
- Our current provider's fallback slowed us to a lower-capacity model but still had region failover gaps; some requests dropped during DNS TTL expiry.

Current stack: 
- Primary: managed LLM endpoints (company X) in us-west1 and us-east1, autoscaling on GPU instances.
- Caching: minimal application-level prefix caching.
- Observability: internal traces + provider console.

Success criteria for us: 
- Predictable P95 latency < 250ms for the primary auth flow under normal load, P99 < 1s.
- Graceful degradation: if primary model/region is unhealthy, traffic shifts to a fallback with clear SLOs and no dropped requests.
- Clear runbooks and post-incident evidence for compliance.

Attached a CSV extract of incident history. Looking for a short summary from you confirming that Redwood can address these items and proposed next steps (tech deep-dive + SOC2/evidence).

Thanks,
Sarah
Product Ops — Acme Corp

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah@acme.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up from today's call — reliability focus

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear summary and the incident CSV. Below is a concise recap of our understanding + immediate recommendations and next steps. Please flag anything we missed.

Recap (pain & stack):
- Two P0 incidents tied to regional capacity constraints and slow failover.
- Limited prefix/KV caching means more cold-start tokens and higher per-token latency at scale.

What Redwood can provide (high level):
- Smart routing + multi-region active routing: policy-based routing that sends traffic to healthy regions/variants with sub-100ms local decisioning.
- Graceful degradation strategy: prioritized fallback model variants (quantized CPU-ready + smaller GPU model) and automatic region failover with buffered request queues to avoid drops.
- SLOs & SLAs: Standard SLO guidance (we typically target P95 < 200–300ms depending on model family) and enterprise SLA add-ons for uptime and latency guarantees.
- Observability & runbooks: per-route traces, token-level cost/latency breakdowns, and post-incident exportable runbooks for compliance.

Technical suggestions from the call:
1) Fallback model plan: primary = open-llm-x (fp16 on GPU), fallback-1 = open-llm-x-quant (8-bit, GPU/CPU hybrid), fallback-2 = distilled-llm (small CPU-only)
2) Region policy: active-active in us-west/us-east with automatic client-side sticky session fallback; failover TTL < 5s.
3) Caching & batching: enable prefix/KV caching for auth flow; maintain per-tenant cache to reduce cold starts.
4) SLO targets to evaluate: P95 250ms (auth path), P99 1.0s; mitigation: auto-scale + burst buffer for 60s to absorb spikes.

Attachments: redwood-reliability-playbook.pdf (high-level playbook); we pulled the incident-history-export.csv you attached into our assessment.

Next steps (proposed):
- Technical deep-dive (60m) with our runtime/infra leads (Jordan) to validate traffic patterns and model/quantization options.
- Deliver a short runbook template and a proposed rollout plan (canary + A/B) within 5 business days.
- Provide SOC2 evidence pack & compliance checklist after we sign an NDA/partner agreement; we can share the SOC2 report and audit artifacts.

Would Wednesday 7/7 or Thursday 7/8 work for a deep-dive? We can include a small proof-of-concept proposal if you want an isolated test.

Thanks — Ben
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sarah Jones <sarah@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up from today's call — reliability focus

Adding a few technical notes for the deep-dive and the PoC scope: 

- Model variants: recommend having at least two graduated fallback levels (quantized + distilled). Quantized open-llm-x-8bit usually runs on lower-cost GPUs with ~1.2x latency overhead but huge cost savings. Distilled models serve as CPU-only emergency fallback.
- KV cache placement: keep hot-cache in-region with cross-region warm-cache sync every 30s to avoid cold-storms during failover.
- Request buffering: Redwood can configure an elastic buffer for spikes (configurable up to 120s). During buffer drain we mark requests as degraded but not dropped and surface that in traces.
- Health checks & routing: health-check cadence at 5s, probe-based routing with progressive percentage shift (canary-style) to avoid blackholing.
- Compliance artifacts needed early: your internal retention policy, list of audit log recipients, and desired retention window. We can template those items.

I'll bring our runtime engineer to the deep-dive. Happy to prepare a basic config template for the auth route before the call.

— Jordan

From: Sarah Jones <sarah@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-30T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up from today's call — reliability focus

Ben/Jordan — this is great and aligned to what our infra team expects. A couple of clarifications before the deep-dive: 

1) During region failover we need zero request loss (dropping is a showstopper). You mentioned buffered requests — is there a SLA for buffered delivery?
2) For SOC2 and audit artifacts: can you share what is redacted vs the full reports? We need to know if we can present them to our compliance reviewers.

We can do the deep-dive on Thu 2026-07-08 at 10:00am PT. Please send a calendar invite and any pre-read. Also include a short POA for the PoC (success criteria, timeline).

Thanks,
Sarah

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-30T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up from today's call — reliability focus

Perfect — confirmed: Thu 2026-07-08 10:00am PT for the technical deep-dive. Calendar invite sent (see link). Quick answers to your clarifications: 

1) Buffered delivery: we never drop in-buffered mode as long as buffer capacity is configured for the route. For enterprise SLA we can guarantee delivery attempt and surface exact delivery time windows; we'll include explicit RTO/RPO language in the SLA addendum for the PoC.
2) SOC2: we provide a redacted SOC2 report for initial review, and under a standard NDA we can share more detailed artifacts and evidence. If you need platform logs for an audit, we can arrange a read-only access plan with scoped retention.

Deliverables before the call (we'll send these by EOD Monday 07/05): 
- PoC POA (success criteria + timeline + acceptance tests)
- Runbook template and proposed fallback model mapping
- Redacted SOC2 report & compliance checklist

If anything else comes up, ping me directly. Looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Ben
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
